verdict.rationale: The evidence shows no region or residency selection for hosted Cal.com. The only way to control where data lives is self-hosting the MIT-licensed Cal.diy fork, which promises 'full control over their scheduling infrastructure', and one user reports self-hosting both the API and the database. That workaround has real caveats: Cal.com says Cal.diy is not for enterprise or production use and has stopped publishing Docker images. Missing for 10: a documented region/residency choice on the hosted service (e.g. EU/US data location), a production-supported self-host path, and residency-specific documentation (GDPR compliance claims are not residency controls).
